LESSON: AREA

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.1 Circles (5 lessons) • circumference of a circle • length of an 
Topic 3.2: Area
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area, part of Measurements 3.1 Circles (5 lessons) • circumference of a circle • length of an  in Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use area in real-life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. calculate the area of circles in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. work out the area of a sector of a circle in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. work out the surface area of cubes and cuboids in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. work out the surface area of a cylinders in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. determine the surface area of a triangular prism in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Area in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. work out the area of irregular shapes using

   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem solving: as the learner uses cut outs of sectors of circles from locally available materials and

find out the area of the sector.

• Learning to learn: as the learner uses models to find the surface area of cubes, cuboids and cylinders and derive the formulas

for each.
